blocks.title: How to identify your skin type
blocks.subtitle: Two quick checks — no dermatologist needed

items.a: Wash your face, wait an hour, and press a tissue on your forehead and cheeks. If the tissue turns see-through and greasy all over, your skin is oily. You may also notice shine within an hour of washing and larger-looking pores.
After washing, your skin feels tight and sometimes flaky, especially on the cheeks. The tissue stays dry with almost no oil, and makeup or moisturiser can sting slightly on application.
The tissue shows oil on the T-zone (forehead, nose, chin) but stays clean on the cheeks. This is the most common type — oily in the middle, normal or dry at the edges.
Your skin reddens, tingles or stings easily with new products, heat or sun. Patch-test anything new on your inner arm for 24 hours before using it on your face.
You can also visit a skin specialist (dermatologist) for a proper assessment, especially if you have persistent acne, rosacea or pigmentation. A 10-minute consultation removes all the guesswork.

blocks.title: Does this suit your skin type?
blocks.text: Oily and combination skin: yes, this is a strong fit. Normal skin: fine as a light daily serum. Dry skin: use it with a richer moisturiser on top. Very sensitive skin: patch-test first, and start with alternate days.
